items.title: Sands interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2019
items.q: I went to school with Sam Harris... We were in school at the same time... met in a practice room at Manhattan School of Music.

ctx.x: Is that the — pretty much the only way for young musicians now to take the jazz path?

No, I won’t say that’s the only way, but it is a good way to meet other musicians and to form these connections with people that are around your same age. You know, I mean if I didn’t go to college or Manhattan School of Music or a conservatory would I still be in the position I am today? I’m sure I would be. But I think I would have had a lonelier time getting there versus now, now I have colleagues, now I have people that I graduated with that we play music together, or I see them in other bands around as we’re…

and so we met in a practice room at Manhattan School of Music. That was the first time we met, and that was like four o’clock in the morning. So you don’t really get that if you don’t go to school you know. But not to say that you won’t ever meet another musician you know, but there is a certain thing that comes with going to schools and learning and being in classes and being around other people that are also very creative and then you never know what happens.
